name: Undersea cables & GPS
summary: Finnish court convicts Fitburg crew over Baltic cable damage; no new cable cut found as of 10 Nov
state: A Helsinki court on 5 Nov convicted the Fitburg's Russian captain and a crew member of sabotage over cable damage in the Gulf of Finland on New Year's Eve, jailing the captain (Euronews); the ruling can be appealed. Denmark's Bornholm station had logged 30 GPS jamming and spoofing incidents in 2026 by 10 Aug, against 16 in all of 2025 (European Pravda). Searches to 10 Nov found no new cable cut, and the ruling concerns a past incident, so Watch holds.
for_you: GPS interference around the Baltic can affect flights and shipping; airlines and crews have procedures for it. Cable incidents rarely cut internet access for users in Europe because traffic reroutes.
rubric_hit: Cable damage incident (Fitburg sabotage conviction, 5 Nov) and persistent Baltic GNSS interference

sources.title: Euronews — Finnish court jails Russian captain over Baltic Sea cable sabotage
European Pravda — Denmark records GPS disruptions at record levels near island of Bornholm

why: Subsea cables carry ~99% of intercontinental data; GPS jamming affects aviation and shipping.
drivers: Anchor drags, sabotage, conflict-zone jamming and spoofing.

rubric.alert: Multiple cable cuts isolating a region, or confirmed sabotage.
rubric.watch: Cable damage incident, or widespread GNSS interference affecting aviation.
rubric.normal: No new cable cuts or major jamming escalations.
